about: The Hobie 16's running rigging and deck hardware (docs/hobie16-7, slice 6): the mainsheet's 6:1 between the traveller car on the rear crossbar and the boom's block hanger, the traveller line, the jib cars on the front crossbar's track and the jib sheet, the jib's and main's downhauls, the outhaul, the halyards' tails and the mast base's cleats. hardware_hobie16.py draws them on slices 2-5's platform, rig and sails, sheeted for upwind on starboard tack. Blender's frame (X forward, Y to port, Z up), metres, the design waterline with the crew aboard at z 0. Assemblies and counts from Hobie's parts guide and the class rules (specs_hobie16.json class_facts); sizes from common dinghy hardware of the kind (no brand's model is copied).

mainsheet.note: 6:1 blocks between the rear crossbar's traveller car and the boom's block hanger, on a 35 ft line (class_facts.mainsheet). 10 mm rope.
mainsheet.note_hanger: Where the block hanger sits on the boom is solved, not set: the sheet leans 10 deg aft of square from the traveller car to it. One owner's trampoline, 89.5 in between the crossbars' insides (Hobie's forum), puts the crossbars where slices 2-5 have them (2.23 m here), and a 9 ft foot from a gooseneck on the mast then reaches 0.6 m past the rear crossbar. Sheeted hard, H16 crews pull the 6:1 two-blocked (the blocks touching), which can only happen with the hanger nearly over the car: hung at the clew, the sheet would lean 71 deg off square and the blocks could never meet. So the hanger is a bail under the boom some way forward of its end, and the clew's outhaul runs on to the end cap.
mainsheet.note_sheaves: The standard system was a 57 mm triple with a ratchet below and a 40 mm triple above (the Hobie class association's page on the H16 mainsheet; since 2022 a block made for the boat replaces them). The model's blocks are generic shapes of those sizes, no maker's design.
mainsheet.note_blocks: Both blocks are triples (6:1): three grooved sheaves side by side on an athwartships axle, cheek plates between and outside them, a strap, swivel and shackle to the fitting each hangs from. The upper one has a becket for the sheet's dead end and hooks through a bail riveted under the boom; the lower one, on the traveller car's swivel post (through an eye on its top), carries a cam cleat on an arm forward. The six parts leave each sheave fore and aft.
mainsheet.note_tail: The tail leaves the lower block's cam through its fairlead, forward and up toward the crew, lies along the trampoline toward the helm's hand and the spare is flaked in a loose pile. A stand-up spring round the swivel holds the lower block upright, and each block's D-shackle hooks round its fitting's wire (round review 1: a gap at the boom and an open hook).

traveller.note: The car rides the rear crossbar's deep track, centred under the boom for upwind, with end stops near the corner castings. Owners on Hobie's forum describe the control line through rollers on the car to a cleat and fairlead on the crossbar, with a stopper knot so the car can't slam into the casting; the arrangement varies by year. Drawn: a 7 mm line from each end of the car along the crossbar's top to a cam cleat near each corner, a figure-eight stopper inboard of it, the tail lying forward on the trampoline (class_facts.rear_crossbar).

jib_sheet.note: Rule 2.3: the jib cars run in the FRONT crossbar's track, locked by a spring plunger. The sheet is 2:1 a side and one line: an owner on Hobie's forum gives its path as from the becket on the jib car up to the block on the jib, back to the car and through its swivel cleat; the other side the same. So the clew carries a double block, each car a becket and a ratchet block with a cam over it, and the tail runs across the trampoline between the cars. The working (port) side is tight, the lazy (starboard) side slack. 8 mm rope; owners give the sheet as about 32 ft. The cars sit a little outboard of the clew (0.32 m to port) so the sheet pulls down and out.

downhauls.note: The jib's tack downhaul to the bridle plate (two parts), and the main's downhaul (cunningham): class_facts.boom allows up to 6:1; drawn as a 4:1 between two 24 mm doubles, the upper with a becket hooked to a ring under the gooseneck, the lower with a cam on the mast foot's eye, its tail falling aft to the trampoline.

outhaul.note: From a ring at the clew aft round a sheave in the boom's end cap, forward along the boom's port side to a cam cleat 0.45 m from the end, the tail hanging in a bight (class_facts.boom: the outhaul cleats on the boom).

halyards.note: Both sails hang on hooks (the main's at the masthead, the jib's at the hounds), so the halyards are slack once hooked: each tail runs down the mast's side to its cam cleat on the mast's foot and is coiled and hung there (class_facts.mast). The jib's head ties to a short wire from the hounds.
